story-info.story-title: Implement Factorial Specification and Proofs Homework 2: Recursion and Loops ready-for-dev

technical-requirements.proof-mode: Most proofs can use `nonlinear_arith` mode: `proof fn f(..) by (nonlinear_arith)`

code-structure.pattern: Follow triangle example pattern from Chapter 4

spec-pattern.step: 1. Define recursive spec function with decreases clause
4. Implement iterative exec function with loop invariant

library-framework-requirements.no-external-crates: All functionality must use vstd library only

file-structure-requirements.verification-block: All code must be inside `verus! { }` block

development-testing.note: Can write normal `#[test]` functions and use `cargo test` to verify implementations before attempting proofs
development-testing.pattern: Write tests first to ensure implementations work, then add proofs

verification-requirements.requirement: All proof functions must complete successfully
All exec functions must verify against their spec
Recursive implementation must verify when `factorial(n as nat) <= usize::MAX`
Iterative implementation must verify when `factorial(n as nat) <= usize::MAX`

proof-pattern.guidance: Control flow in proofs should follow control flow of specification
proof-pattern.technique: Use `assume(false)` to develop proof path by path
Use `assert` to identify where Verus is stuck, then apply lemmas

monotonicity-proof.lemma-usage: If not using nonlinear_arith, use `lemma_mul_inequality` directly after recursive call

loop-invariant-pattern.requirement: Loop invariant must bound the iteration variable
Loop invariant must relate to post-condition in ensures clause
Use monotonic lemma for overflow/underflow reasoning

critical-constraints.constraint: Must follow triangle example pattern exactly
Monotonic lemma is REQUIRED for both recursive and iterative implementations
Overflow protection: Only verify when `factorial(n as nat) <= usize::MAX`
Loop invariants do NOT inherit pre-conditions - must state explicitly

common-pitfalls.pitfall: Forgetting decreases clause in spec function
Not using monotonic lemma for overflow reasoning
Loop invariant that doesn't relate to post-condition
Not following control flow of specification in proofs
Forgetting to use lemma_mul_inequality if not using nonlinear_arith

success-criteria.criterion: All implementations return same value as spec
